reviewedPartitions.outputs: client and server API projections whose generated contract emissions are identical, with explicit group/endpoint naming and omitted custom transports
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: contract drift fails generation-equivalence tests; middleware declares typed request/session failures; runtime HTTP failures belong to generated clients/handlers
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: declarative contract/build-time generation; no persistent runtime state in the contract projection itself
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: bounded schema/contract compilation; actual HTTP clients own network resources separately
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: All six residual INT rows are source-identical, and INT-008 already owns a narrower event-wire compatibility slice. Generated contract identity cannot be assigned to one residual row by number or status.

reviewedPartitions.outputs: canonical decoded DTOs and typed event stream including durable metadata
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: protocol decode failure terminates the Effect event stream with ClientError; transport errors belong to the provided HttpClient
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: per-client runtime and per-subscription stream lifetime
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: network/HTTP/SSE lifetime; custom PTY WebSocket transport is explicitly outside the generic HTTP client
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: Event wire fidelity is already implemented under INT-008 and frozen. Broader network client ownership among the six generic residual rows is not source-grounded.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: typed integration list/get/key/OAuth/attempt requests and credential/auth payloads
reviewedPartitions.outputs: Integration service projections, NoContent mutations or normalized InvalidRequestError auth/code failures
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: authorization failures are intentionally normalized; completion distinguishes code-required from auth failure
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: delegated to the core Integration service and its connection/attempt state
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: HTTP request scope plus provider-specific auth/network/credential lifetimes delegated beneath the handler

reviewedPartitions.inputs: PTY id and location scope, the x-opencode-ticket: 1 token-mint header, optional short-lived ticket and replay cursor query values, plus WebSocket text or binary terminal input frames
reviewedPartitions.outputs: a scoped one-time connect token or a WebSocket stream that emits bounded replay chunks, an absolute-cursor control frame and live PTY output while forwarding valid UTF-8 client input to the attached PTY
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: token mint rejects a missing or invalid CSRF header/origin with ForbiddenError and a missing PTY with PtyNotFoundError; connect rejects a missing pre-upgrade PTY with 404 and an invalid/disallowed ticket with 403; post-upgrade missing/exited attach closes with code 4404; invalid UTF-8 binary input is dropped; socket close/errors terminate the transport path while detach is ensured
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: tickets live in a global cache for at most 60 seconds and are consumed atomically once only when ptyID/directory/workspaceID scope matches; each WebSocket attachment lives until the socket/drain race ends and is detached in finalization
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: ticket state is capped at 10,000 entries and replay strings are split at 65,536 JavaScript string units per frame, but the server WebSocket outbox is explicitly unbounded and graceful-shutdown socket tracking remains a TODO, so an end-to-end bounded native transport lifetime is not established
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: The six residual INT rows remain one generic source-indistinguishable class. Core PTY/ticket paths also overlap the already accepted opencode.process-terminal owners, while the server transport requires HTTP/WebSocket/auth authority and still has an unbounded outbox plus unresolved graceful-shutdown tracking. No residual INT id can own this boundary by subtraction.

adjacentAcceptedOwnership.conclusion: The PTY domain/process lifecycle is already mapped entirely to accepted process-terminal owners. Integration decomposition may describe the server/custom-transport seam but cannot re-own accepted PTY lifecycle semantics.

disqualifiers: All six residual INT rows have the same generic story, no requirements and the same integration surface.
INT-009's not-started status does not create semantic ownership distinct from the five in-progress peers.
INT-008 already owns event-wire compatibility and INT-004 owns a scoped integration slice, so broad contract generation cannot re-own those behaviors.

historyReview.limitation: Pinned current contract evidence is used directly; unavailable historical intent and differing controller status are not converted into task semantics.

closureCriteria: Each residual INT owner requires task-specific source, caller, direct test and genuine spec evidence that distinguishes it from the six-row equivalence class; task number, controller status and generated endpoint order are insufficient.
Any network/transport candidate must explicitly own credentials, authentication, reconnect/timeout/failure behavior and resource lifetime and must not re-own INT-004 or frozen INT-008 behavior.
INT-002 remains frozen for repository side effects and INT-010 remains governed by the enterprise-remote missing-spec record unless materially new pinned evidence resolves those blockers.

The PTY WebSocket/ticket boundary remains blocked until task-specific evidence distinguishes a residual INT owner and explicitly resolves the unbounded outbox, graceful-shutdown lifetime and server auth/network authority without re-owning accepted process-terminal behavior.
All reviewed and unresolved rule partitions must receive source-grounded task dispositions or remain blocked before the integrations family can be called decomposed.
